topic: ssc examinee from barguna aims to be magistrate
headline_marked: Barguna student [[scores highest in Humanities for SSC]], dreams of becoming a magistrate
headline: Barguna student scores highest in Humanities for SSC, dreams of becoming a magistrate
summary: Kathmoni Haldar, a top performer from Betagi Girls School and College, shared her aspirations at a GPA-5 reception ceremony in Barguna.
details: Kathmoni Haldar, a student of Betagi Girls School and College, achieved the highest marks in the Humanities group in Barguna district for the SSC examinations.
Speaking at a GPA-5 reception ceremony organized by Prothom Alo and Shikho at the District Shilpakala Academy, she expressed her dream of becoming a magistrate.
The event also honored other high achievers, including Afia Umme Salma from Bamna Upazila Asmatul Necha Secondary School, who traveled from the Pirojpur border to attend.
Principal Ziaul Karim of Syed Fazlul Haq Degree College encouraged students, stating that being children of the coast should not limit their intellectual potential.
He further emphasized the correct use of information technology, advising students to utilize AI (Artificial Intelligence) without letting AI control them.
The ceremony, themed 'Dream Big, Build Life,' is being held across 64 districts to honor SSC and equivalent exam GPA-5 achievers.
The event concluded with musical performances by young artist Dipu Rahan and his team, which saw enthusiastic participation from the students.
caption:
From the coast to the courtroom: a top SSC performer in Barguna dreams of becoming a magistrate.

Kathmoni Haldar, a student of Betagi Girls School and College, achieved the highest marks in the Humanities group in Barguna district for the SSC examinations.

Speaking at a GPA-5 reception ceremony organized by Prothom Alo and Shikho at the District Shilpakala Academy, she expressed her dream of becoming a magistrate.

The event also honored other high achievers, including Afia Umme Salma from Bamna Upazila Asmatul Necha Secondary School, who traveled from the Pirojpur border to attend.

Principal Ziaul Karim of Syed Fazlul Haq Degree College encouraged students, stating that being children of the coast should not limit their intellectual potential.

He further emphasized the correct use of information technology, advising students to utilize AI (Artificial Intelligence) without letting AI control them.

The ceremony, themed 'Dream Big, Build Life,' is being held across 64 districts to honor SSC and equivalent exam GPA-5 achievers.

The event concluded with musical performances by young artist Dipu Rahan and his team, which saw enthusiastic participation from the students.

#Barguna #SSC #Education #SuccessStory #Bangladesh

Source: Prothom Alo

topic: businessman beaten to death in chuadanga
headline_marked: Chuadanga: [[Businessman beaten to death]] after being called to a house
headline: Chuadanga: Businessman beaten to death after being called to a house
summary: A 40-year-old chop-pyaju businessman named Chayon was allegedly killed in Alamdanga, Chuadanga, after being lured to a residence.
details: A 40-year-old chop-pyaju businessman named Chayon was allegedly beaten to death in Osmanpur village, Hardi Union, Alamdanga, Chuadanga, on Tuesday afternoon.
According to the family, Chayon was called to the house of a man named Helal around 11 AM on Tuesday morning via mobile phone.
The family alleges that Chayon was detained and beaten at the house. Later, Helal's family contacted Chayon's son, Maruf, claiming money was owed and asking him to bring three stamps to the house.

When Maruf and his grandfather arrived at the house in the afternoon, they were told that Chayon had committed suicide. However, the body was later transported to the Alamdanga Upazila Health Complex (Hardi Hospital) via a van.
Chayon's son, Maruf, stated that they had a family relationship with Helal's family and that any outstanding debts would have been paid, questioning why his father was killed.

Dr. Rubayed Hassan, an emergency department physician at Hardi Hospital, confirmed that Chayon had died before arriving at the hospital and that there were signs of injury on various parts of his body.
Alamdanga Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Rakibul Islam stated that police have visited the scene and the body has been sent to Chuadanga Sadar Hospital morgue for an autopsy.
caption:
A businessman was lured to a house and allegedly beaten to death in Chuadanga, while suspects allegedly claimed he committed suicide.

A 40-year-old chop-pyaju businessman named Chayon was allegedly beaten to death in Osmanpur village, Hardi Union, Alamdanga, Chuadanga, on Tuesday afternoon.

According to the family, Chayon was called to the house of a man named Helal around 11 AM on Tuesday morning via mobile phone.

The family alleges that Chayon was detained and beaten at the house. Later, Helal's family contacted Chayon's son, Maruf, claiming money was owed and asking him to bring three stamps to the house.

When Maruf and his grandfather arrived at the house in the afternoon, they were told that Chayon had committed suicide. However, the body was later transported to the Alamdanga Upazila Health Complex (Hardi Hospital) via a van.

Chayon's son, Maruf, stated that they had a family relationship with Helal's family and that any outstanding debts would have been paid, questioning why his father was killed.

Dr. Rubayed Hassan, an emergency department physician at Hardi Hospital, confirmed that Chayon had died before arriving at the hospital and that there were signs of injury on various parts of his body.

Alamdanga Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Rakibul Islam stated that police have visited the scene and the body has been sent to Chuadanga Sadar Hospital morgue for an autopsy.
